channel.title: Pawstcard Journal
channel.description: Practical notes for independent pet sitters and dog walkers: client updates, visit report cards, and running a solo pet-care business.

item.title: How Should an Independent Pet Sitter Set Rates?
item.description: A practical way for independent pet sitters to set rates: count your costs and time, price by visit type, explain the number, and review it once a year.

item.title: How Pet Sitters Can Ask for Reviews and Referrals Without Awkwardness
item.description: When and how independent pet sitters can ask clients for reviews and referrals: good timing, short sample messages, and what to avoid.

item.title: Sitting Multiple Pets: How to Update Clients on Each One
item.description: How to plan visits and write updates for multi-pet households: separate routines, one note per pet, and how to handle tension between pets.

item.title: Pet Sitting Medication Log: How to Record Doses Clearly
item.description: How pet sitters can handle medication instructions and keep a simple dose log: what to confirm, what to record, and when to call the client or vet.

item.title: How Long Should a Pet Sitting Drop-In Visit Be? 15, 30, or 45
item.description: How to choose and explain drop-in visit lengths: what fits in 15, 30, and 45 minutes, and how to avoid promising more than the visit can hold.

item.title: How to Write a Pet Sitting Cancellation Policy Clients Respect
item.description: A plain-language guide to pet sitting cancellation and late-change policies: what to include, how to word it kindly, and when to make exceptions.

item.title: Pet Sitter House Key Handoff: A Home Access Checklist
item.description: How pet sitters can handle house keys and entry codes: agree how access is shared, test it before the trip, and write down the return plan.

item.title: Pet Sitting Emergency Plan: What to Put in Writing Before a Stay
item.description: What a pet sitting emergency plan should cover: vet contacts, spending authorization, backup people, and how to message a client in a crisis.

item.title: How to Manage Holiday Pet Sitting Bookings Without Burning Out
item.description: How independent pet sitters can plan holiday bookings: set limits, clear policies, and a booking calendar so busy weeks stay manageable.

item.title: What Information Should a Pet Sitter Collect From Pet Parents?
item.description: A pet sitter's intake list: the details to collect from pet parents before a job, how to store them, and what to keep out of your records.

item.title: Pet Sitting Meet-and-Greet Checklist: What to Ask and Observe
item.description: A practical meet-and-greet checklist for pet sitters and dog walkers: what to ask, what to watch, and what to agree on before the first visit.

item.title: How Independent Pet Sitters Build Client Trust (and Keep It)
item.description: Trust is built before, during, and after each job. A practical checklist for independent pet sitters, including how to report problems well.

item.title: What to Write in Pet Sitting Updates When Nothing New Happens
item.description: Long stays make updates repetitive. Nine ideas for fresh, honest pet sitter notes, plus how to keep them short when the day was uneventful.

item.title: Pet Sitter Photo Updates: How Many to Send and What to Shoot
item.description: How many photos to send per visit, which three shots matter, and how to take them quickly without letting your phone take over the visit.

item.title: How to Write a Pet Sitting Visit Report Clients Actually Read
item.description: A simple five-part structure for pet sitting visit reports, with a checklist, a sample note, and the mistakes that make clients stop reading.
